examples.en: In summer, we rode a rubber boat in the valley.
The kids are having fun on the rubber boat.

examples.ko: 고무보트에 바람을 넣는 데 오래 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took a long time to pump air into the rubber boat.

examples.ko: 파도가 센 날에는 고무보트를 타면 위험해요.
examples.en: Riding a rubber boat on a day with strong waves is dangerous.
The rescue team saved people using a rubber boat.

examples.ko: 고무보트는 가벼워서 혼자서도 옮길 수 있어요.
examples.en: A rubber boat is light, so you can carry it by yourself.

explain: 사람이 안에 앉아서 타는 배라서 몸에 끼는 '튜브'와는 달라요. 바람을 넣어 쓰기 때문에 '바람을 넣다, 타다' 같은 말과 함께 나와요.
explain_en: You sit inside it like a boat, so it differs from a '튜브' that you wear around your body. It is inflated, so it goes with '바람을 넣다' and '타다'.

examples.en: It suddenly poured on my way home.

examples.ko: 늦은 밤 혼자 걷는 귀갓길이 무서워요.
examples.en: The walk home alone late at night is scary.
The subway on the way home is always crowded.
The route home in front of the school has been made safe.
They patrol for the children's safe walk home.
Walking with a friend makes even the way home enjoyable.

explain: '퇴근길'은 일을 마치고, '하굣길'은 학교를 마치고 가는 길인데, 귀갓길은 어디서든 집으로 돌아가는 길이라 더 넓게 써요. 밤길 안전 이야기에서 특히 자주 들려요.
explain_en: '퇴근길' is the way home after work and '하굣길' after school, but 귀갓길 covers going home from anywhere. It is often heard in talk about safety on night streets.

examples.ko: 급정거 때문에 뒷좌석에 둔 짐이 앞으로 쏟아졌어요.
examples.en: Because of the sudden stop, the bags on the back seat spilled forward.

examples.ko: 아이가 갑자기 뛰어나온 탓에 급정거가 불가피했어요.
examples.en: A child suddenly ran out, so a sudden stop was unavoidable.
The bus stopped suddenly and the passengers staggered.

examples.ko: 택시가 갑자기 급정거하는 바람에 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: The taxi suddenly braked hard and I was startled.

examples.ko: 앞차가 급정거할 때를 대비해서 거리를 두세요.
examples.en: Keep your distance in case the car ahead stops suddenly.

examples.ko: 그 차가 급정거했지만 늦어서 가볍게 부딪혔어요.
examples.en: That car braked hard but too late, and they bumped lightly.

explain: 자동차나 버스가 갑자기 서는 상황에 써요. '급정차'와 거의 같은 뜻이고, 급브레이크를 밟아 확 서는 장면에 잘 어울려요. 사람이 갑자기 멈출 때는 '갑자기 멈춰 서다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is used when a car or bus stops suddenly. It is almost the same as '급정차' and fits scenes of slamming the brakes. When a person stops abruptly, say '갑자기 멈춰 서다'.

en: a point on the way; chokepoint; corner of a road

examples.en: I waited for my friend at the corner in front of my house.
There is a bakery on the way to the market.
Cars were jammed at the narrow passage.
As we enter the start of winter, the weather turns chilly.
If you pass that spot, you can see the sea.
People stood at every corner and watched.

explain: '길목'은 길이 꺾이거나 어디론가 들어가는 중요한 지점이에요. '골목'은 집들 사이의 좁은 길이라서 달라요. '여름의 길목', '봄의 길목'처럼 계절이 바뀌는 때를 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: 길목 is an important point where a road bends or leads into somewhere. 골목 is a narrow lane between houses, so it is different. It can also mean the time when seasons change, as in 여름의 길목 or 봄의 길목.

examples.ko: 비행기에서 내려다보니 땅이 까마득히 멀어 보였어요.
examples.en: Looking down from the plane, the ground looked incredibly far away.
I looked up at the dizzyingly tall building.

examples.ko: 어릴 적 일이라 까마득히 잊고 있었어요.
examples.en: It happened in my childhood, so I had completely forgotten it.

examples.ko: 그때 일은 까마득히 먼 옛날 이야기 같아요.
examples.en: That time feels like a story from the distant past.
The summit is still a long, long way off.
I totally forgot about the appointment.

explain: '아득히'와 비슷하게 거리나 높이가 매우 멀 때 쓰고, 시간이나 기억에도 써요. '까마득히 잊다'처럼 완전히 잊었다는 뜻으로도 자주 말해요.
explain_en: Like '아득히', it is used when distance or height is very great, and it also applies to time and memory. It is often used in '까마득히 잊다' to mean having forgotten something completely.

examples.ko: 차선을 바꿀 때 끼어들기를 하면 위험해요.
examples.en: Cutting in when changing lanes is dangerous.
A sudden cut-in nearly made me hit the car ahead.

examples.ko: 줄을 설 때 끼어들기는 예의가 아니에요.
examples.en: Cutting in when waiting in line is bad manners.
It's a road with a lot of cutting in, so I drove slowly.
It was a no-cutting-in zone, so I just drove past.

examples.ko: 운전할 때는 끼어들기에도 신호를 꼭 켜야 해요.
examples.en: When driving, you must also use your signal when cutting in.

explain: 동사 '끼어들다'에서 나온 말로, 운전 중 차선에 끼어드는 것과 줄에 끼어드는 것에 모두 써요. 줄 서기에서 순서를 어기고 앞에 서는 것은 '새치기'라고도 하고, 둘 다 좋지 않게 보는 행동이에요. 운전 이야기에서는 도로 표지판에도 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It comes from the verb '끼어들다' and covers both cutting into a lane while driving and cutting into a line. Breaking the order in a queue is also called '새치기', and both are seen as rude. In driving contexts it often appears on road signs.

examples.ko: 내리막길에서 브레이크를 세게 밟았더니 차가 끼익 소리를 냈어요.
examples.en: When I hit the brakes hard on the downhill road, the car screeched.

examples.ko: 이 산업은 십 년 전에 이미 정점을 지나 내리막길에 들어섰어요.
examples.en: This industry passed its peak ten years ago and is already on the decline.
Slow your bike down on downhill stretches.
The street in front of my house slopes downhill, so it's slippery in winter.
Going up is hard, but the way down is quick.

examples.ko: 요즘 그 가수는 인기가 내리막을 걷고 있어요.
examples.en: These days that singer's popularity is on the decline.

explain: 반대말은 '오르막'이에요. 길뿐 아니라 인기나 경기가 나빠지는 때를 '내리막길을 걷다'처럼 비유로도 말해요.

phrases.example: 그 회사는 몇 년째 내리막길을 걷고 있어요.
phrases.en: That company has been in decline for several years.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실제 길이 아니라 인기, 실적, 건강이 점점 나빠지는 상황을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It does not refer to an actual road but to popularity, performance or health steadily getting worse.

explain_en: The opposite is '오르막' (uphill). Besides roads, it is used figuratively for a time when popularity or the economy is getting worse, as in '내리막길을 걷다'.

examples.en: The ship dropped anchor in the harbor.
The sailors raised the anchor and set off.
The anchor caught on the bottom and the boat stopped.

examples.ko: 이 가게 로고는 작은 닻 모양이에요.
examples.en: This shop's logo is shaped like a small anchor.

examples.ko: 친구가 닻 모양 목걸이를 선물로 줬어요.
examples.en: My friend gave me an anchor-shaped necklace as a gift.

examples.ko: 폭풍이 오자 닻을 더 깊게 내렸어요.
examples.en: When the storm came, they let the anchor down deeper.

explain: 닻은 배가 흘러가지 않게 물속으로 내리는 무거운 쇠 도구예요. 배를 멈출 때는 '닻을 내리다', 출발할 때는 '닻을 올리다'라고 해요. 한곳에 자리 잡고 정착하는 것도 비유로 '닻을 내리다'라고 말해요. 소리는 [닫]이에요.
explain_en: A 닻 is the heavy iron tool lowered into the water so a ship won't drift. You stop with '닻을 내리다' and set off with '닻을 올리다'. Figuratively '닻을 내리다' also means settling down in one place. It is pronounced [닫].

examples.en: The cow suddenly charged toward us.

examples.ko: 버스가 가게 앞으로 돌진해서 큰일 날 뻔했어요.
examples.en: The bus rushed toward the shop, and it almost became a disaster.
The player charges forward with the ball.
He is someone who charges toward his goals.
My friends rushed inside as soon as the door opened.

examples.ko: 멈추지 않고 돌진하면 다칠 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you charge without stopping, you can get hurt.

explain: '달리다'는 그냥 빠르게 움직이는 것이고, '돌진하다'는 앞에 뭐가 있어도 멈추지 않고 세게 들어가는 거예요. 동물, 차, 운동선수가 주어일 때가 많고, 사람의 의욕을 말할 때도 써요.
explain_en: 달리다 just means moving fast, while 돌진하다 means pushing forward hard without stopping for whatever is ahead. The subject is often an animal, vehicle, or athlete, and it can also describe a person's drive.

examples.en: The rear tire of my bike went flat.
The rear tire got a puncture, so I went to the repair shop.

examples.ko: 트럭 뒷바퀴가 진흙에 빠져서 움직이지 않았어요.
examples.en: The truck's rear wheel got stuck in the mud and wouldn't move.

examples.ko: 뒷바퀴 위에 짐받이가 달린 자전거를 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought a bicycle with a luggage rack over the rear wheel.

examples.ko: 아이의 두발자전거는 뒷바퀴에 보조 바퀴가 붙어 있어요.
examples.en: The child's bike has training wheels attached to the rear wheel.
I replaced the rear wheel with a new one and it rides much more smoothly.

explain: '앞바퀴'와 짝이 되는 말이에요. 자전거, 오토바이, 자동차 모두에 쓸 수 있어요. 바퀴가 아니라 타이어 쪽 문제를 말할 때도 '뒷바퀴에 바람이 빠졌어요'처럼 자연스럽게 말해요.
explain_en: It pairs with '앞바퀴' (front wheel) and works for bicycles, motorbikes and cars. When the problem is with the tire, people still naturally say things like '뒷바퀴에 바람이 빠졌어요'.

examples.en: I went into a maze at the amusement park and got lost.
The hallways of this building are like a maze.
The children are solving a maze puzzle.

examples.ko: 미로의 출구를 찾는 데 한 시간이 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took an hour to find the exit of the maze.
The market alleys are as complicated as a maze.

examples.ko: 이 미로에서 빠져나갈 길이 안 보여요.
examples.en: I cannot see a way out of this maze.

explain: 놀이공원 시설뿐 아니라 '미로 같은 골목'처럼 복잡해서 헤매는 곳이나 상황을 비유할 때도 많이 써요. '길을 잃다', '미로를 빠져나가다'와 같이 쓰면 자연스러워요.
explain_en: Besides the amusement-park attraction, it is often a metaphor for a confusing place or situation, as in '미로 같은 골목'. It sounds natural with '길을 잃다' and '미로를 빠져나가다'.

en: make an emergency landing; make a forced landing

examples.en: The plane made a forced landing on a small island.
In the movie, a spaceship crash-lands on a strange planet.
Where should you make an emergency landing if the engine stops?
There was an accident in which a helicopter made a forced landing in the mountains.

examples.ko: 불시착한 뒤에도 승객들은 침착하게 구조를 기다렸어요.
examples.en: Even after the forced landing, the passengers waited calmly for rescue.
Because of the blizzard, we nearly had to make a forced landing.

explain: '불시착하다'는 '-에 불시착하다'처럼 내린 곳에 '에'를 써요. 정상으로 내리는 '착륙하다'와 달리 고장이나 날씨 때문에 예정과 다르게 내렸다는 느낌이 들어 있어요. 뉴스에서 자주 들려요.
explain_en: You mark the place with '에', as in '-에 불시착하다'. Unlike the ordinary '착륙하다', it implies landing differently from plan because of a breakdown or weather. It is common in news reports.

examples.ko: 장마철에는 비탈의 흙이 흘러내릴 수 있으니 조심하세요.
examples.en: During the rainy season, soil on slopes can slide down, so be careful.

examples.ko: 이 도시는 평지가 적어서 건물이 비탈을 따라 지어져 있어요.
examples.en: This city has little flat land, so buildings are built along the slopes.
I fell while riding a bike on a slope.

examples.ko: 우리 집은 비탈 위쪽에 있어서 겨울에 오르기 힘들어요.
examples.en: Our house is at the top of the slope, so it is hard to climb in winter.
My grandfather cultivated a small field on the slope.
The slope was so steep that it was hard to push the stroller.

explain: 주로 '산비탈'처럼 산이나 언덕의 기울어진 곳을 말해요. 길이 기울어져 있으면 '비탈길'이라고 하고, 형용사 '비탈지다'도 함께 알아 두면 좋아요.
explain_en: It mostly appears as '산비탈', a slanted part of a mountain or hill. When it is a sloping road, people say '비탈길', and the adjective '비탈지다' is worth learning too.

examples.ko: 절 마당에 오래된 석탑이 서 있어요.
examples.en: An old stone pagoda stands in the temple yard.
I looked at stone pagodas in Gyeongju.
They say this stone pagoda is over a thousand years old.
We took a photo in front of the stone pagoda.
Snow piled up on top of the stone pagoda.
I visited a temple famous for its stone pagoda.

explain: 탑은 재료에 따라 돌로 만든 석탑, 나무로 만든 목탑, 벽돌로 만든 전탑으로 나눠요. 한국은 석탑이 특히 많아요. 불국사의 석가탑과 다보탑이 대표적이에요.
explain_en: Pagodas are divided by material: 석탑 (stone), 목탑 (wood), and 전탑 (brick). Korea has especially many 석탑. 석가탑 and 다보탑 at Bulguksa are the best-known examples.

examples.ko: 여행 중에 유명한 스타디움 투어를 했어요.
examples.en: On my trip I took a tour of a famous stadium.

examples.ko: 경기 시작 전에 스타디움 앞에서 만나요.
examples.en: Let's meet in front of the stadium before the match starts.

examples.ko: 경기 날에는 스타디움이 사람들로 가득 찼어요.
examples.en: On match day the stadium was full of people.
This stadium holds fifty thousand people.
There are many good restaurants near the stadium.

examples.ko: 그 가수는 큰 스타디움에서 콘서트를 열었어요.
examples.en: That singer held a concert at a big stadium.

explain: 일상에서는 '경기장'이 더 흔하고, 스타디움은 이름에 붙이거나 크고 멋진 경기장을 말할 때 자주 써요. '운동장'은 학교나 동네의 넓은 땅이라 느낌이 달라요. 종목을 붙여 '야구장', '축구장'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: In daily talk '경기장' is the more common word; 스타디움 shows up in names and for big, impressive venues. '운동장' is a school or neighborhood field, so it feels different. You can also add the sport: '야구장' (baseball field), '축구장' (soccer field).

examples.en: Let's meet in front of the clock tower.

examples.ko: 역 광장에는 큰 시계탑이 서 있어요.
examples.en: A big clock tower stands in the station square.
The clock tower bell told us it was noon.

examples.ko: 학교 시계탑은 십 년 전에 지어졌어요.
examples.en: The school's clock tower was built ten years ago.
At night the clock tower is lit up.
On my trip I saw a famous clock tower.

explain: 학교, 역, 광장에 세운 시계가 달린 탑이에요. 약속 장소를 정할 때 '시계탑 앞에서 만나요'라고 많이 말해요. 런던의 빅벤 같은 유명한 시계탑도 같은 이름으로 불러요.
explain_en: It is a tower with a clock at a school, station, or plaza. People often use it as a meeting spot: 시계탑 앞에서 만나요. Famous clock towers abroad, such as the one known as Big Ben in London, are also called 시계탑.

examples.en: Be sure to keep a safe distance from the car ahead.

examples.ko: 비 오는 날에는 안전거리를 더 길게 두어야 해요.
examples.en: On rainy days, you should leave a longer safe distance.

examples.ko: 안전거리를 확보하지 않으면 사고가 날 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you don't keep a safe distance, an accident can happen.
The distance was so short that I got a scare.

examples.ko: 운전 학원에서 안전거리 유지하는 법을 배웠어요.
examples.en: I learned how to keep a safe distance at driving school.

examples.ko: 사람들 사이에 안전거리를 두고 서 주세요.
examples.en: Please stand with some safe distance between people.

explain: 운전할 때 앞차와 부딪히지 않도록 띄워야 하는 거리를 가장 먼저 떠올려요. '확보하다', '유지하다', '지키다'와 자주 같이 써요. 사람들 사이에 필요한 거리를 말할 때도 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: It most often brings to mind the distance you must leave from the car ahead so you don't collide. It pairs with verbs like '확보하다', '유지하다' and '지키다'. It can also refer to the space needed between people.

examples.en: The way home is a steep hill road.

examples.ko: 아이들이 송아지를 끌고 꼬부라진 언덕길을 올라오고 있어요.
examples.en: The children are coming up the winding hill road, leading a calf.

examples.ko: 언덕길에서 자전거를 타면 내려갈 때 조심해야 해요.
examples.en: When you ride a bike on a hill road, you have to be careful going down.

examples.ko: 눈이 오면 언덕길이 미끄러워서 차가 못 다녀요.
examples.en: When it snows, the hill road is slippery and cars can't get through.
Every evening I take a slow walk along the hill road in my neighborhood.

examples.ko: 언덕길 끝에 작은 카페가 하나 있어요.
examples.en: There is a small cafe at the end of the hill road.

explain: '오르막길', '내리막길'은 가는 방향에 초점이 있고, '언덕길'은 언덕에 나 있는 길 자체를 말해서 오르내리는 길 모두를 가리켜요. 그래서 올라갈 때도 내려갈 때도 '언덕길'이라고 할 수 있어요.
explain_en: '오르막길' (uphill road) and '내리막길' (downhill road) focus on the direction you travel, while '언덕길' refers to the road on a hill itself, so it covers both going up and coming down.

examples.en: The kids are running up and down the stairs.

examples.ko: 엘리베이터가 고장 나서 오르락내리락 걸어 다녔어요.
examples.en: The elevator broke, so I walked up and down the stairs.
The stock price moved up and down all day.
The boat rocked up and down on the waves.
My fever kept going up and down, so I went to the hospital.
I walked up and down the mountain path and my legs hurt.

explain: 위로 올라갔다 아래로 내려갔다를 되풀이하는 모습을 나타내요. 계단이나 산길뿐 아니라 가격, 체온, 기분처럼 변하는 것에도 써요. 보통 '오르락내리락하다'로 동사처럼 많이 써요.
explain_en: It shows something repeatedly going up and then down. It is used not only for stairs and mountain paths but also for things that fluctuate, like prices, body temperature and mood. It is also very often used as the verb '오르락내리락하다'.

examples.en: Avoid secluded alleys at night.
We wandered only through secluded back alleys.

examples.ko: 공원 안쪽은 으슥해서 혼자 가기 무서워요.
examples.en: The inside of the park is secluded, so it's scary to go alone.
A strange sound came from a hidden place.
After sunset, the forest path became gloomy and secluded.

examples.ko: 으슥한 길에서는 휴대폰을 보며 걷지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't walk looking at your phone on a secluded road.

explain: 사람이 별로 없고 구석져서 조용하며 조금 무서운 곳에 써요. '으슥한 골목/길/곳'처럼 뒤에 장소가 오는 경우가 많아요. 단순히 조용한 곳을 말하는 '한적하다'와 달리 불안한 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: It describes a place with few people, tucked away, quiet and a little scary. It is often followed by a place word, like '으슥한 골목/길/곳'. Unlike '한적하다', which just means quiet, it carries a feeling of unease.

examples.en: The electric pole fell backward because of the typhoon.

examples.ko: 전봇대 옆에 쓰레기를 버리면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not throw trash next to the electric pole.
I bumped my head on an electric pole while walking.
Flyers are plastered on every electric pole.
The meeting spot is in front of the blue electric pole.
Please park the car so it avoids the electric pole.

explain: '전신주'라는 말도 있지만 말할 때는 '전봇대'가 더 편하고 흔한 느낌이에요. 약속 장소를 알려 줄 때 '파란 전봇대 앞'처럼 길 표시로도 많이 써요.
explain_en: There is also the word '전신주', but '전봇대' feels more casual and natural in speech. People also use it as a landmark when giving directions, like '파란 전봇대 앞'.

examples.ko: 제트기가 큰 소리를 내며 하늘을 날았어요.
examples.en: A jet flew through the sky with a loud roar.
A jet is much faster than an ordinary plane.
I saw a private jet at the airport.

examples.ko: 이 제트기는 열 명만 탈 수 있어요.
examples.en: Only ten people can ride this jet.
Since I was little, my dream was to be a jet pilot.
At the exhibition I climbed aboard an old jet.

explain: 일상에서는 그냥 '비행기'라고 하고, 제트기는 제트 엔진을 단 빠른 비행기를 따로 말할 때 써요. 싸우는 군용 비행기는 '전투기', 사람을 태우는 큰 비행기는 '여객기'예요.
explain_en: In daily life people just say 비행기, and 제트기 is used when specifically meaning a fast plane with a jet engine. A military fighting plane is a 전투기 and a large passenger plane is a 여객기.

examples.en: The car speeds down the highway.
The horse raced across the wide field.
A motorcycle is speeding through the night streets.
The kids play, dashing across the playground.
It is dangerous to speed through and ignore the signal.

examples.ko: 기차가 어둠 속을 질주하는 모습이 멋졌어요.
examples.en: The sight of the train racing through the dark was great.

explain: '질주하다'는 '달리다'보다 속도가 크고 힘찬 느낌이 있어요. 차, 말, 기차 같은 것에 많이 쓰고 사람이 달릴 때는 '전력 질주하다'처럼 말해요. 가볍게 달릴 때는 '뛰다'나 '달리다'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: 질주하다 feels faster and more forceful than the plain '달리다'. It is mostly used for cars, horses and trains, while for a person you say '전력 질주하다'. For light running '뛰다' or '달리다' is more natural.

examples.en: Two cars collided at the intersection.
Our opinions often clash.

examples.ko: 약속 시간이 서로 충돌해서 만날 수 없어요.
examples.en: Our appointment times conflict, so we can't meet.
There are many accidents where birds hit windows.

examples.ko: 두 사람이 크게 충돌한 뒤 말을 안 해요.
examples.en: After the two people had a big clash, they don't talk.

examples.ko: 일정이 충돌하지 않게 미리 확인해 주세요.
examples.en: Please check ahead so the schedules don't conflict.

explain: '충돌하다'는 물건끼리 부딪힐 때도, 사람의 생각이나 일정이 안 맞을 때도 써요. 가볍게 몸이 닿을 때는 '부딪히다'를 쓰고 '충돌하다'는 크고 세게 부딪히는 느낌이에요. 일정이나 의견이 맞지 않을 때는 '겹치다', '맞지 않다'도 많이 말해요.
explain_en: 충돌하다 is used both when objects crash and when opinions or schedules conflict. For light contact, 부딪히다 is used, while 충돌하다 feels bigger and harder. For schedules and opinions, 겹치다 or 맞지 않다 are also common.

examples.en: The stairs are narrow and steep, so you have to be careful.
The elevator was broken, so I went up by the stairs.
Kids are playing at the bottom of the stairs.
I came down those stairs slowly, one step at a time.
I left my umbrella at the end of the stairs.

examples.ko: 이 건물 층계는 폭이 넓어서 안전해요.
examples.en: The stairs in this building are wide, so they are safe.

explain: '계단'과 거의 같아서 바꿔 써도 돼요. 다만 '층계'는 조금 글 같은 느낌이 있어서, 대화에서는 '계단'이라고 말하는 사람이 많아요. '층계를 오르다/내려오다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It is almost the same as '계단', so you can swap them. '층계' feels a bit more literary, and many people say '계단' in conversation. You say '층계를 오르다' (go up) or '층계를 내려오다' (come down).

examples.en: I saw a big trailer truck on the highway.
The trailer truck is heading to the port with cargo.
My uncle drives a trailer truck.

examples.ko: 뒤에 트레일러가 붙은 차는 속도가 느려요.
examples.en: A vehicle with a trailer attached is slower.
The road was blocked because of a trailer accident.
We rented a camping trailer and travelled.

explain: 트레일러는 짐을 싣기 위해 트럭 뒤에 연결하는 큰 차량이에요. 한국에서는 짐을 싣는 큰 트럭을 말할 때 가장 많이 쓰고, 캠핑카처럼 뒤에 끌고 다니는 '캠핑 트레일러'도 있어요. 영화 예고편을 뜻하는 'trailer'는 한국어로 보통 '예고편'이라고 해서 구별해요.
explain_en: A teureilleo is a large vehicle attached behind a truck to carry cargo. In Korea it mostly refers to big cargo trucks, though a 캠핑 트레일러 pulled behind a car also exists. A movie trailer is usually called 예고편, which keeps the two meanings apart.

examples.en: It is dangerous to cross a road without a traffic light.
He crossed the United States by bicycle.
The children cross the street with their hands raised.

examples.ko: 배로 바다를 횡단하는 데 열흘이 걸려요.
examples.en: It takes ten days to cross the sea by ship.

examples.ko: 동물들이 도로를 횡단하지 못하게 울타리를 쳤어요.
examples.en: They put up a fence so animals cannot cross the road.

examples.ko: 신호가 바뀌면 횡단할 수 있으니까 조금만 기다려요.
examples.en: You can cross once the signal changes, so let's wait a moment.

explain: '건너다'보다 딱딱한 글 말투예요. '횡단보도', '대륙 횡단'처럼 굳은 말에서 자주 보여요. 길을 건널 때 일상에서는 '건너다'가 훨씬 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It is more formal than '건너다'. You see it in set words like '횡단보도' (crosswalk) and '대륙 횡단'. For crossing a street in daily life, '건너다' sounds much more natural.
